title: Harden default signaling worker: open-relay abuse bound + Origin/CORS check (task 1353 follow-up)
description:
Security review of task 1353 (commit d3ad44c) found the new default-deployed Cloudflare signaling worker (workers/signaling/, wss://signal.dash.jxh.io) is an UNAUTHENTICATED, OPEN relay with no abuse bound. E2E encryption is intact (verified: room key k stays in the URL fragment, is only fed to WebrtcProvider as 'password' -> deriveKey AES-GCM client-side, NEVER transmitted; the server relays only opaque encrypted publish payloads and cannot decrypt; no secrets committed; opt-in posture preserved). These are abuse/cost gaps, not confidentiality leaks:

1) NO rate-limiting / connection cap / abuse bound. The single global Durable Object (idFromName('signaling')) accepts unlimited WebSocket upgrades and unlimited subscribe/publish from ANY client. Anyone on the internet can use signal.dash.jxh.io as a free pub/sub relay for arbitrary rooms (it is a drop-in y-webrtc server with no allowlist of room ids), and a flood of connections/topics is a DoS + Cloudflare-billing risk now that it is the DEFAULT endpoint the deployer pays for. y-webrtc public servers are conventionally open, but a self-deployed default warrants at least: a per-DO connection/topic cap, a max message size, and ideally a basic per-IP rate limit. Consider Cloudflare's built-in rate-limiting or a token-bucket in the DO.

2) NO Origin/CORS restriction. fetch() upgrades any websocket request regardless of Origin; the relay is usable by any web origin, not just the dash app. Consider checking the Origin header on the upgrade (allowlist the dash app origin(s)) to reduce third-party free-riding. (Note: Origin is spoofable by non-browser clients, so this only deters casual browser-based abuse; combine with #1.)

3) MINOR: wrangler.toml sets [observability] enabled=true. Worker app code emits no console.* (no message contents/room-ids/IPs logged by us), but CF platform observability records sampled request metadata + uncaught exceptions. Acceptable, but document the privacy scope (room id is sent as the y-webrtc topic in PLAINTEXT over the WS, and peer IPs are inherently visible to a WebRTC signaling/relay server) in docs/37-collab.md so deployers know the metadata the server observes.

Privacy scope confirmation for the doc: the signaling server observes the 128-bit random room id (the y-webrtc topic, sent plaintext) + peer IPs only; it never sees doc bytes (P2P over WebRTC DTLS) nor the room key k. The collabLink.ts comment claiming the server 'never sees the room id either' is slightly overstated -- the fragment isn't sent over HTTP, but the room NAME IS sent as the WS subscribe/publish topic; worth a one-line correction.

Files: workers/signaling/src/index.ts (fetch/webSocketMessage), workers/signaling/src/relay.ts, workers/signaling/wrangler.toml, packages/authoring-ui/src/collab/collabLink.ts (comment), docs/37-collab.md.
